text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- There can be no printing of money to fulfil the demands for wage increases put forward by the striking teachers' negotiating team, the Serbian government and trade union said in a statement. Negotiators said the government's wage increase offer was insufficient.
- Delegation of Hungarian Workers' party headed by party president Gyula Tirmer is on a three-day visit to Yugoslavia at the invitation of the League of Communists Movement for Yugoslavia.
- Main board of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia accuses some opposition leaders of trying to gain power at all costs and destabilise the country.
- Croatian Foreign Minister Mate Granic will pay a one-day working visit to Belgrade at the invitation of his Yugoslav counterpart Milan Milutinovic.
- Yugoslavia's industrial output rose 2.9 percent in January year on year and fell 20.8 percent from December 1996, according to the federal statistics office.
- Yugoslav Prime Minister designate Radoje Kontic will soon propose the new cabinet members to be endorsed by the federal parliament.
- Students will continue their demonstrations until all their demands are met and extend support to striking teachers.
- The equivalent of $300,000 was stolen from the Dutch airline KLM's Belgrade office in an armed robbery on Monday.
- Belgrade university deans still negotiating with newly-appointed Education Minister Jova Todorovic to resolve student demands for the dismissal of the university rector.

- New round of bilateral talks on succession of the former Yugoslavia started in Brussels on Monday with only one subject, division of archives of the former federal state. Yugoslav delegation led by Jovan Popovic, director of Yugoslav archives.
- Textile and leather industry workers announce a general strike on February 25, demanding reduction of taxes and credits for launching production.
- The Belgrade City transport drivers decide to suspend strike started on Monday after management promised to pay their outstanding wages on Tuesday.
- Serbian government funnels 20 million dinars from its budget for schools in Vojvodina, for teachers' outstanding wages, the republican finance ministry said.
- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic talks with OSCE Bosnia chief Robert Frowick about preparation for local elections.
